audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers read Fiora, Skill, Gnar, Gnar, Fiora, Gnar, Gnar. The Fiora-side mirror already flipped its chart to Fiora, Fiora, Fiora, Skill, Fiora, Skill, Gnar as one atomic group, and this page's own whys say the same thing — whys[1] 'she still edges level 2', whys[2] 'she keeps level 3', whys[3] 'it's a coinflip', whys[5] 'it stays a skill check'.
audit.why: Gnar has no hard CC until the Mega transform, so Lunge (13/11.25/9.5/7.75/6s) closes his poke for free through the early levels and Riposte blanks whatever he throws next; the item stages are genuinely even, and 2+ items is Gnar's on GNAR! wall value.
audit.corrected: Level 2 -> Fiora, Level 3 -> Fiora, Levels 4-5 -> Skill, First item -> Skill on both layers; Level 1, Level 6 and 2+ items already matched.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer's phase whys were generic boilerplate with no numbers — 'Rage management is the champion', 'Full kit online' — and never gave Riposte's cooldown despite telling the reader to track it.
audit.why: Riposte is 24/22/20/18/16s, the longest cooldown in her lane kit and the entire reason a Gnar can commit at all; Hop is 22s at rank 1 and GNAR! is 90s at rank 1, which is what makes a wasted transform so expensive.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written into the level-2, level-3, 4-5 and first-item stages and the cooldown block.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer described Riposte only as 'Parries + stuns. Bait it.' — it never said what triggers the stun, so the reader has no way to know that their own Wallop is what arms it. Vitals were never described as percent-max-health true damage on that layer either.
audit.why: Riposte parries all incoming damage and disables, then stabs: the stab slows, or stuns if she blocked an immobilizing effect. Wallop is immobilizing, so a telegraphed Wallop into an up Riposte hands her the stun. Duelist's Dance heals her on every Vital hit, and Grand Challenge's Vital damage ignores resistances.
audit.corrected: The trigger condition and the healing/true-damage consequences are now stated in the cooldown block, the do's, the don'ts, the interactions report and itemization.

edits.after: Your Hyper third-hit is the one Mini window, but she Lunges in and Ripostes the follow-up — she edges 2.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Riposte's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Form RNG: with Mega up Wallop answers her Lunge, but caught in Mini with Hop (22s) down she dashes on and Ripostes you.

edits.before: Stridebreaker is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Riposte's cooldown.

notes: Chart flips are one atomic group across both layers and copy the Fiora-side mirror exactly, so the two directions agree. The content layer here was already at the approved bar and needed nothing; all the damage was in the full layer, which was boilerplate with 'Riposte' pasted in and never said what arms its stun — your own Wallop.
